pr_body:
Fixes #5493. Fixes T-1036.

Mutating process.env properties can't be supported if we still want to statically replace them with their values at build time. In source code this is flagged as an error. In node_modules it is a warning in case the code isn't actually used at runtime. In that case, the behavior won't be as expected but at least it will compile.

In order to do this, the diagnostics in Rust now have a severity property, which can be `Error`, `Warning`, or `SourceError`. `SourceError` means error if `asset.isSource` and warning otherwise.

Also fixed an error message for script tags which had a copy/paste mistake I noticed.

issue_context.title: Broken output for `delete` on an process.env property
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

Don't replace `delete process.env.SOMETHING` with `delete undefined;`

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

Remove the whole statement or replace with an empty statement.

## 😯 Current Behavior

`delete undefined;` is invalid in strict mode. This is even verified by terser.

## 💁 Possible Solution

`process.env.*` is inlined here: https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/a4cf3e958ea1136b4829eb93615fba5328213471/packages/transformers/js/src/visitors/process.js#L26

This special case is described by `t.isUnaryExpression(path.parent, {operator: 'delete', argument: node})`.
comments: @mischnic I'd love to pick up this issue
@alphabet-codes sure, feel free to work on this

review_comments: Do we still want to allow mutations with computed properties?? Seems weird to allow that but not static properties.
It will always be possible to mutate them anyway by assigning `process.env` to a variable and then changing that.

Sure, but the process.env object won't have any properties besides the ones added at runtime, so it's not great to rely on that anyway. IMO better to be consistent when it's not assigned to a variable unless there's a really good reason to allow this.
